Note::TexAccessor::align_blocks¶

Back to Note Tex Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::align_blocks() const

Extract Complete Alignment Environments¶

align_blocks() finds complete align and align* environments in every Text cell. Each token includes its \begin{...} and matching \end{...} markers, so it can be inspected, stored, or passed to another TeX operation without reconstructing the environment name.

Matches retain source order, including when starred and unstarred forms are interleaved. The extractor spans newlines, accepts any body content up to the matching closing marker, and ignores unrelated environments. An incomplete environment is not emitted; this method extracts valid lexical blocks rather than repairing them.

The ragged result follows the standard TokenBatch contract. tokens() is a rank-1 Text Note of all blocks. offsets() is a rank-1 Int64 Note of length source.numel() + 1; flattened source cell i owns tokens in [offsets[i], offsets[i + 1]). Cells without a block therefore produce equal adjacent offsets. Source rank is represented by those lane boundaries rather than copied onto the variable-length token result.

The receiver is not mutated. Extraction is linear in source bytes plus regex matching cost and allocates the matched blocks and offsets. Undefined produces an undefined token Note with offsets [0]. Only Text is accepted; Bytes and native dtypes reject.

Example 1: Starred And Unstarred Blocks Keep Document Order¶

const auto documents = pluss::make_note({
    R"(before \begin{align*}a&=1\end{align*} middle \begin{align}b&=2\end{align})",
    "no alignment here",
    R"(\begin{align}c&=3\end{align})"});
const auto blocks = documents.tex().align_blocks();

std::cout << blocks.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["\\begin{align*}a&=1\\end{align*}", "\\begin{align}b&=2\\end{align}", "\\begin{align}c&=3\\end{align}"]

Example 2: Offsets Recover Per-Cell Ownership¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < blocks.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << blocks.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 2, 3]

Cell 0 owns two blocks, cell 1 owns the empty interval [2, 2), and cell 2 owns the final block.

Example 3: Native Dtypes Reject¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().align_blocks();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "align Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

align Int64: rejected
